items.guidance: Read the s6-overlay service directories that the Dockerfile installs and separate the one-shot init-* steps from the long-running services. If the long-running set has a web server, a Celery worker, a Celery beat scheduler, a document consumer, and Redis, use the web server as the image command, declare the other three as Procfile lines, and report Redis as Deployz-provided Valkey. Run the needed init steps before each command.

Classify the contents of /usr/src/paperless/data (for example a search index, a classifier model, or a SQLite file, which may be rebuildable or replaced by PostgreSQL) separately from the media directory that holds original and archived documents. Before you change code, check whether the settings support an S3 storage backend for media (for example through django-storages) and report those setting names if they exist.

The npx prisma migrate deploy evidence may come from a Node frontend or tooling package, while psycopg points to a Python backend, so check whether a Prisma schema exists in the runtime stage at all. If the backend is Django, check whether the s6 init scripts already run manage.py migrate at startup, and whether that command runs in the runtime stage as it is. Report which result applies.

Search for the Celery app module and check the s6-overlay service run scripts for the celery worker and celery beat commands. Report those exact commands with their working directory and user, whether beat runs as a separate process, and which Redis URL setting the broker reads, so the vendor can map it to REDIS_URL.
